rationale: Interpreted the no-snapshot receipt and closed that child question. Receipt bdf2837a4c004f95b6c9b19db4fb8154 evaluated all four comparisons: after a restart with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs of a node holding no snapshot, the reported configuration is empty (violated twice, as an id list and as a server count of zero), while the same restart without the feature reports {A,B,C} (holds twice). The mechanism is the parent question's scan start combined with the eager replay, and the consequence is stronger than a stale membership: the node comes up with no membership at all. I acquired the election gate that governs what such a node does next and recorded the account, including the two source-derived consequences I did not execute.

interpretations.rationale: The declared predicate is that a node restarted with the feature rebuilds its membership from the configuration entry in its log even when it has no snapshot; the witness contradicts it in both forms. Admission index 0 records the fixture: cluster {A,B,C} with B leading, node A holding zero snapshots, a staged commit index of 11 over a log ending at 12, and A reporting {A,B,C} while running. After A is restarted with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs (event index 1) it returns, replays to index 13, and reports an empty configuration - neither the id list nor the server count matches the bootstrap membership (comparisons 0 and 1 violated). The control restart without the feature (event index 2) reports {A,B,C} with three servers (comparisons 2 and 3 hold). Mechanism: the scan starts at max(lastSnapshotIndex, lastApplied)+1, restoreFromCommittedLogs has already raised lastApplied to the persisted commit index (api.go 724-753, raft.go 1296-1363), and with no snapshot lastSnapshotIndex is zero, so every configuration entry in the log lies below the scan start and processConfigurationLogEntry is never called (api.go 610-620); the FSM replay still consumes those entries as ordinary commits. Consequences derived from source, not executed here: with latestIndex zero the node's heartbeat timeout logs 'no known peers, aborting election' and never transitions to candidate (raft.go 225-246), and its vote handling skips the membership check for an empty configuration, so it grants votes to candidates it does not know (raft.go 1660-1680). Limits: the observation is a construction state with a 300ms settle, in-memory stores with scaled timeouts, a graceful shutdown, and the node held no snapshots because the harness never took one rather than because of a store failure; the election and vote behaviours remain source-derived.
limitations: The empty configuration is observed at construction; the node's subsequent refusal to campaign and its vote grants are derived from source, not executed.
The absence of snapshots is arranged by the harness (ten-minute interval, none taken) rather than caused by a store failure.
In-memory stores, scaled timeouts and a graceful shutdown; one run per mode.
counterevidence: The identical restart without the feature rebuilds {A,B,C}, so the empty configuration is not a property of the stores or of the restart procedure.
The node's FSM did replay the log to index 13, so the empty configuration is not explained by missing log entries.
